Phenotype → Mechanism

Which smallest changes are sufficient to reproduce your observations?

Try the Science Advances HK validation

This benchmark starts from WT and uses only simulated HK readouts plus fixed N and pFusion during inference. Published kinetic parameters are revealed afterwards for comparison. It tests parameter recovery within the same simulator, not agreement with independently measured data.

1 Reference

K/B values come from your reference model. You do not need mutant K/B values.

2 Measured constraints

Unchecked values remain at WT. N means total release sites, not the readily releasable pool estimate. Locked values cannot change during inference or attribution.

3 Describe the phenotype

Choose only what you observed. Unknown measurements carry no weight.

Additional measurements
EPSC train values

Numeric train values can accompany either input mode. Each non-missing pulse receives equal weight.

Measurement conditions

SS = mean last five responses / P1. Recovery = (probe − last-five mean) / (P1 − last-five mean), branching from the full post-conditioning state. P1 absolute units are released vesicles; use a ratio for EPSC amplitude comparisons if quantal size is unchanged.

4 Find candidate mechanisms
Advanced search settings

Checked parameters are inferable. Others are WT-constrained. Bounds are absolute; defaults are 0.1–10× WT for rates, 0–10× for slopes, 0.2–5× for time constants.

Qualitative target ranges (ratio to WT)

The final upper bound may be blank for no upper limit.

Your reference simulator and its parameters stay unchanged.

Start with what you can measure

Enter directions or numbers, lock known parameters, and compare candidate mechanisms. The analysis distinguishes fit quality from mechanistic simplicity.

Rates will be inferred by the model. You can inspect them after the comparison.
